text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; please describe exactly where the pain is located and how quickly it started. REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint while swelling in the right ring finger is very suggestive of an issue with the extensor tendon. Please describe any history of trauma, repetitive gripping, or use of vibrating tools for this hand. REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound of the right hand DIP joint; REQUEST IMAGES for any previous X-rays of the right hand.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound of the right hand DIP joint: Tendon thickening and hypoechoic areas suggestive of partial extensor tendon tear; increased fluid around the DIP joint. Previous X-ray of the right hand: No fractures or dislocations visible; soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Extensor Pollicis Longus (EPL) Tendon Tear (Mallet Finger) of the right ring finger.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
